headline: Sunny, dry and milder-than-normal weather lasts through Saturday, but a coastal storm could bring a windy, soaking rain to New York City and the surrounding area Sunday afternoon into Monday morning.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday night is clear and calm in New York City, with light west-northwest winds under strong high pressure. Overnight lows will be set mainly by heat escaping under the clear skies. Patchy freezing fog is likely in river valleys, sheltered inland spots and the Long Island Pine Barrens, bringing a low chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday through Saturday stay mostly sunny and dry, with highs several degrees above normal in the upper 50s to mid 60s. Nights turn a few degrees milder than normal by late week, especially in the city and right along the coast. Freezing fog is possible again Thursday night in valleys and sheltered inland areas, when the black ice risk on bridges and overpasses is a bit higher; a weak upper-level disturbance passing Thursday night into Friday morning won't bring any rain.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A low-pressure system forming off the Southeast coast is expected to move north near Cape Hatteras Sunday morning and then pass over or near the area late Sunday into Monday morning; the National Hurricane Center gives it a 40% chance of becoming a tropical or subtropical system. If it tracks close, it could bring a windswept, soaking rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning, with a 30–50% chance of at least 1 inch of rain in 24 hours, a 20–30% chance of 2 inches, and under a 10% chance of 3–4 inches, plus a low, localized flash flood threat. Winds could reach 20–30 mph with gusts of 35–40 mph if the storm hugs the coast, while a track farther southeast would limit wind and coastal impacts. Drier, seasonable weather likely follows later Monday into early next week.

coast: Calm conditions continue on the waters through Sunday morning, with northwest to west winds under 15 knots and ocean seas of 2–3 ft. Small Craft Advisory or possibly gale conditions could develop later Sunday into Monday, depending on the coastal storm's track and strength; the strongest winds are most likely over the ocean waters southeast of Long Island. Minor coastal flooding is possible early next week with the approaching new moon, mainly if the storm tracks over or west of the area.
watch_for: The track and strength of the Sunday–Monday coastal storm, which will decide how much rain, wind and coastal flooding New York sees.
Whether the storm becomes tropical or subtropical (40% chance per the National Hurricane Center).
Patchy freezing fog and possible black ice on bridges and overpasses outside the city tonight and especially Thursday night.
confidence: Forecasters are highly confident in dry, mild weather through Saturday, increasingly confident a coastal storm will affect the area Sunday into Monday, but have low confidence in its exact track, strength, rain totals and winds.
